ours-decoding.short: Night School's attention model, sampled for this film
ours-decoding.citation: media/school/decoding/facts.json, written by tools/school/fill_decoding.mjs from system/school/decoding.mjs and corpus-grammar.mjs: 1,500 continuations per setting from three prompts with shared random streams, judged by a parser of the corpus generator's own rules.
claims: From the prompt 'pylon', greedy decoding writes 'found a kettle . pylon put a cone on the kettle . pylon found a kettle ...'.
Grammatical share from 'pylon': temperature 0.5 0.9807, 1 0.8907, 1.5 0.5107, 2 0.106; top-k 3 0.9487; top-p 0.9 0.9447, 0.5 0.9973; uniform 0; generator 1.
Distinct continuations per run from 'pylon': temperature 1 0.988, top-p 0.5 0.14.
After 'tallow found a': kettle's share is 0.197 at temperature 0.5 and 0.110 at temperature 2; top-k 3 keeps kettle, map and crate; top-p 0.9 keeps 9 words.
Temperature 0.01 reproduces greedy in 200 of 200 runs.
Model perplexity of its own temperature-1 runs from 'pylon': 1.873; of the generator's runs: 1.921.
ours-decoding.n: 1,500 continuations per setting per prompt; three prompts; one model.
ours-decoding.interval: Binomial standard error about 0.013 near a share of 0.5.
ours-decoding.does_not_prove: That any setting is best for large models or human text.

fan2018.short: Fan, Lewis and Dauphin 2018, Hierarchical Neural Story Generation
fan2018.citation: Fan, A., Lewis, M., Dauphin, Y. (2018). Hierarchical Neural Story Generation. ACL 2018. arXiv:1805.04833.
fan2018.read: full text read by the core sub-agent; to be re-read by the fact-check
claims: Stories are generated by sampling from the k = 10 most likely words (top-k sampling); beam search tends to produce common, repetitive phrases.

holtzman2020.short: Holtzman and others 2020, The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration
holtzman2020.citation: Holtzman, A., Buys, J., Du, L., Forbes, M., Choi, Y. (2020). The Curious Case of Neural Text Degeneration. ICLR 2020. arXiv:1904.09751.
holtzman2020.read: full text read by the core sub-agent; to be re-read by the fact-check
claims: Nucleus (top-p) sampling samples from the smallest set of most likely words whose total probability reaches p.
Maximization-based decoding such as greedy and beam search produces repetitive text; pure sampling from the full distribution produces incoherent text through the unreliable low-probability tail.

factcheck: Independent fact-check 2026-10-15 (FACTCHECK.md): 21 correct, 6 reword, 2 wrong. Wrong: 'ours does not show it' (4 percent of temperature-1 runs hold a word pair unseen in training, and top-p 0.9 removes them) and 'plain spinning works' (11 percent break the rules); the tail segment now says so. Six rewordings applied; distinctTexts and unseenPair added to facts for the reworded lines.
